steps.title: Prepare 4 M LiCl solution
steps.instruction: Add 17.0 g LiCl powder to 50 mL sterile deionized water in a sterile 100 mL bottle, dissolve completely, then bring the volume to 100 mL with sterile water; store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 20 % glucose stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 200 g glucose in 500 mL deionized water, stir until clear, bring volume to 1 L with water, filter‑sterilize through a 0.2 µm Nalgene bottle‑top filter; store as 20 % glucose solution.

steps.title: Prepare 2 % sorbitol stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 20 g sorbitol in 500 mL deionized water, stir until clear, bring volume to 1 L with water, filter‑sterilize through a 0.2 µm Nalgene filter; store as 2 % sorbitol solution.

steps.title: Prepare 0.25 M Na₂CO₃ solution
steps.instruction: Add 2.65 g Na₂CO₃ to 50 mL sterile deionized water in a sterile 100 mL bottle, dissolve completely, then bring volume to 100 mL with sterile water; store at room temperature.

steps.title: Make synthetic dropout powder
steps.instruction: Weigh the amino acids listed (total 55.4 g) and grind together in a clean mortar until homogeneously white; store in an amber bottle at room temperature, protected from light.

steps.title: Prepare SCD liquid medium
steps.instruction: To 500 mL deionized water add 10 g succinic acid, 6 g NaOH, 5 g ammonium sulfate, 1.7 g yeast nitrogen base (without amino acids), and 1.13 g synthetic dropout powder, stirring after each addition until dissolved; bring volume to 900 mL, split into two 1 L flasks, autoclave (121 °C, 15 psi, 30 min), cool, then add 100 mL filter‑sterilized 20 % glucose (to 2 % final) and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare YPD liquid medium
steps.instruction: To 500 mL deionized water add 10 g yeast extract and 20 g peptone, stir until dissolved, bring volume to 900 mL, split into two 1 L flasks, autoclave (121 °C, 15 psi, 30 min), cool to 40–50 °C, add 100 mL filter‑sterilized 20 % glucose (to 2 % final), mix gently, store at room temperature; do not autoclave glucose‑containing medium.

steps.title: Make YPD agar plates
steps.instruction: Prepare YPD liquid as above, autoclave, cool to 40–50 °C, add 100 mL filter‑sterilized 20 % glucose and 20 g agar, mix, pour 25 mL per sterile Petri dish, let cool and dry overnight, store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare LC‑SPO sporulation medium
steps.instruction: To 500 mL deionized water add 6 g potassium acetate, 20 mL 2 % sorbitol stock, 40 mg adenine HCl, 40 mg uracil, 20 mg each of L‑His, L‑Leu, L‑Trp, bring volume to 1 L, split into two 1 L flasks, autoclave (121 °C, 15 psi, 30 min). Immediately before use, take 20 mL aliquot, adjust pH to 8.5 with 0.25 M Na₂CO₃ (add dropwise while stirring and measuring pH); use the medium immediately, do not store.

steps.title: Prepare Nystatin stock in DMSO
steps.instruction: Dissolve 30 mg Nystatin powder in 5 mL DMSO, bring volume to 10 mL with DMSO, mix until fully dissolved, aliquot 1 mL into sterile 1.7 mL microtubes, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Retrieve and streak diploid SK1
steps.instruction: Remove the cryotube containing SK1 diploid cells in 50 % glycerol from the –80 °C freezer, scratch the frozen stock with a disposable loop, streak onto a YPD agar plate, incubate overnight at 30 °C to obtain a dense patch of diploid cells (no sporulation).

steps.title: Create dense cell suspension
steps.instruction: Pick a loopful of cells from the overnight patch, add to 750 µL liquid YPD in a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube, sonicate with a 2‑s pulse at 25 % power (probe 6) ensuring ~95 % cells remain intact.

steps.title: Dilute to OD₆₀₀ 0.06 and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of the sonicated suspension to 950 µL YPD in a 1 mL cuvette (1:20 dilution). Measure OD₆₀₀ of the diluted sample, calculate volume V₁ needed for OD₆₀₀ 0.06 in 3 mL using (OD₆₀₀ × 20) × V₁ = 0.06 × 3 mL; if V₁ < 10 µL, dilute stock 1:10 with YPD and re‑measure. Add the calculated volume of stock to fresh YPD to make 3 mL at OD₆₀₀ 0.06 in a 15 mL Falcon tube, then incubate 23 h at 30 °C, 295 rpm, 45 ° tilt to reach early stationary phase (OD₆₀₀ 1.0–1.3).

steps.title: Prepare microfluidic plate wells
steps.instruction: If any wells are dry, rehydrate them for ≥4 h with storage buffer or sterile deionized water. Using a P‑1000 pipette, remove all storage buffer, then wash each well (except well 1) three times with sterile deionized water, never allowing wells to dry. Rinse well 1 only with sterile water (no wash needed). Remove storage buffer from the culture well and rinse three times with LC‑SPO, leaving 100 µL LC‑SPO to prevent drying.

steps.title: Load media into plate wells
steps.instruction: Add the following volumes to the indicated wells: wells 3–5 → 290 µL LC‑SPO each; well 6 → 290 µL SCD supplemented with 5 % v/v liquid YPD; well 2 → 290 µL sterile deionized water; well 1 → 100 µL 4 M LiCl plus 3 µL 3 mg/mL Nystatin stock (final Nystatin 0.09 mg/mL). Ensure all other wells contain at least 290 µL of storage buffer or the appropriate media to avoid drying.

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension for loading
steps.instruction: After 23 h incubation, open the Falcon tube (foam and pressure released). Verify early stationary phase by OD₆₀₀ 1.0–1.3. Transfer 900 µL of culture to a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube, centrifuge 3 s in a benchtop mini‑centrifuge to pellet clumps. Without disturbing the pellet, pipette 200 µL of the supernatant, place 3 µL on a microscope slide, and confirm ≥80 % of cells are unbudded and no contamination. If clumps remain, repeat spin and check.

steps.title: Load cells into microfluidic well
steps.instruction: Remove LC‑SPO from the loading well (well 1) and add 70 µL of the verified top 200 µL cell suspension.

steps.title: Seal plate with manifold
steps.instruction: Place the vacuum manifold onto the microfluidic plate, ensuring no debris at the interface. Screw vacuum lines securely, press the Seal button on the pump controller, immediately clamp the manifold to the plate using thumbs on top and fingers on bottom (avoid the chamber area), hold for 2–3 s. Successful seal is indicated by pump noise stopping within 10 s; if noise repeats faster than 4 min, re‑clean interface with 70 % ethanol (dry before reuse) and reseal.

steps.title: Mount plate on microscope stage
steps.instruction: Open the CellASIC ONIX2 interface and confirm the plate is sealed. Apply Zeiss immersion oil to the 40× objective. Place the sealed plate on the motorized stage, secure the four corners with modeling clay (or equivalent clamps). Slowly lower the objective onto the plate surface without excessive pressure, then align the microscope. Ensure vacuum lines are routed to avoid strain on the plate during stage movement.

steps.title: Program CellASIC protocols
steps.instruction: In the ONIX2 user interface pre‑load the following protocols: (a) Priming – activate wells 2–6 at 20 kPa for 5 min (well 1 excluded); (b) Cell loading – activate loading well (well 1) at 50.4 kPa for 5 s; (c) Sporulation – activate LC‑SPO wells 3–5 at 8.3 kPa for 48 h; (d) Spore selection/germination – (i) activate well 1 (LiCl‑Nystatin) at 8.3 kPa for 1 h, (ii) activate well 2 (water) at 8.3 kPa for 1 h, (iii) activate well 6 (SCD + 5 % YPD) at 4.2 kPa for ≥8 h; (e) Re‑sporulation – activate well 5 (LC‑SPO) at 8.3 kPa for 48 h.

steps.title: Prime microfluidic plate
steps.instruction: Run the priming protocol: activate wells 2–6 at 20 kPa for 5 min to flush out storage buffer; do NOT activate well 1 (LiCl‑Nystatin) during this step.

steps.title: Focus objective on chambers
steps.instruction: Slowly bring the objective into contact with the plate surface while using the Definite Focus module to achieve sharp focus on the microchamber features; avoid applying excessive pressure.

steps.title: Load cells into chambers
steps.instruction: Execute the cell‑loading protocol: apply 50.4 kPa to the loading well for 5 s. Verify under the microscope that >85 % of cells entering each chamber are unbudded and evenly spread. If loading is insufficient, repeat the loading step; if cells block the entrance, perform a high‑pressure priming step (50.4 kPa, 5 s) to dislodge them.

steps.title: Start sporulation flow
steps.instruction: Activate LC‑SPO wells (3–5) at 8.3 kPa (step F1c) to begin sporulation; maintain pressure at 8.3 kPa ± 0.2 kPa. The 290 µL volume supports up to 48 h of imaging; cells should show size increase without division during the first 12 h and sporulate by 24 h.

steps.title: Monitor sporulation and assess maturity
steps.instruction: After 24 h, examine chambers for mature asci (tight cruciform, linear, or tetrahedral spores with minimal inter‑spore space). If mature spores are absent, the experiment is unlikely to succeed; consider extending LC‑SPO flow up to 48 h.

steps.title: Kill non‑sporulated cells and rinse
steps.instruction: Run the spore‑selection protocol: (a) activate well 1 (4 M LiCl + Nystatin) at 8.3 kPa for 1 h to kill vegetative cells; (b) immediately activate well 2 (sterile water) at 8.3 kPa for 1 h to flush out LiCl‑Nystatin.

steps.title: Induce germination and mating
steps.instruction: Activate well 6 (SCD + 5 % YPD) at 4.2 kPa for at least 8 h. During this period ≥80 % of germination events should be followed by mating (formation of diploid cells). Continue imaging until a new diploid generation is observed.

steps.title: Optional: repeat life‑cycle induction
steps.instruction: After the new diploid generation has divided 1–2 times, stop the current protocol and start the repeated sporulation protocol (step F1e): flow LC‑SPO from well 5 at 8.3 kPa for 48 h, then repeat steps 27–28 (kill non‑sporulated cells, germinate, mate).

steps.title: Acquire time‑lapse images
steps.instruction: Using Zeiss Zen (or equivalent) with the Definite Focus module, set up a multi‑field‑of‑view time‑lapse acquisition (phase‑contrast, 40× objective, fluorescence optional). Follow the manufacturer’s instructions to ensure continuous focus; record images throughout sporulation, selection, germination, and mating phases.
